newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African textile firms fear imports, tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: S.African textile firms fear imports, tariff cuts.

text.p: South Africa's Textile Federation said on Tuesday it wanted to see a judicial inquiry into illegal imports and expressed concern at suggestions tariffs should be cut faster to compensate for a weaker rand.

"The biggest challenege currently facing the South African textile industry is the stream of illegal imports. I intend pursuing the call for a judicial commission of inquiry to examine the issue," said newly-elected chairman Mervyn King.

King also expressed concern at the notion from Finance Minister Trevor Manuel in last week's budget that the government was preparing to accelerate tariff phase-down due to the rand's sharp depreciation.
"Statements of this nature do immeasurable damage to industry confidence during a period of upgrading and considerable capital expenditure as well as technological advancement," he said.

All stakeholders had agreed to a seven-year phase-down in tariff protection with the knowledge that in all probability the rand would depreciate, he said. This factor was therefore built into investment decisions made two years ago.
